LanguageData.DMS_Occultech_RemnantPatterns.label: garrison arsenal
LanguageData.DMS_Occultech_RemnantPatterns.descriptio:
A line of self-supervising sentry weapons built for long-term garrison duty: a quadruped garrison mech for installation security, a large drone platform that flies cover for unmanned mother-drones, and an automated nest that launches FPV suicide drones at intruders. All three were designed specifically for pioneer colonization operations, which needed defenses able to hold a world alone for decades before the fleet arrived, so all three carry fallback directives in their control cores that keep them executing their last standing order until the chassis fails.
Under the laws of war, weapons that outlast the conflict they were deployed for are classed alongside minefields. The remnants still guarding this world's beacons and installations are what these patterns become once their makers are gone.

Approved by ████ and ███, the garrison arsenal and its related technologies are designated class I sealed technology. Sale of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and its related technologies are to be progressively declassified once a colonial world's society attains class I standard.
LanguageData.DMS_Occultech_RemnantPatterns.discovered:
Using the data they have gathered, researchers have finished decoding the sealed technology: the production patterns of two remnant mechs and of the drone hive that garrisoned alongside them.

The bullhound and the Lanius can now be gestated at an automatroid constructor. Gestated units answer to their mechanitor like any other mech, with no limit on their operating range.

The FPV drone hive can now be built. Keep it loaded with steel and it will assemble and launch wildfowl suicide drones.
